scope: R168 end-to-end measurement of the cheap bit-pattern audit candidate
candidate: bit-pattern implementation of the 155 safety checks
reason: the step became slower, not faster, even though the check itself costs less device time
baseline_source: R155 native audit, same harness and configuration

checks_still_running.note: 465 calls are 3 forward passes x 155 audited tensors, the same accounting the harness asserts

the_contradiction: the check itself is cheaper per step than the native one, 4.737 s here against 6.656 s measured in R167, yet the step is 0.75 s slower. Cutting device time inside the check did not translate into step time.
what_this_teaches: R162 removed the audit entirely and the step fell 2.87 s. Replacing it with a cheaper implementation keeps the same per-layer serialisation point, so the scheduler cannot overlap around it the way it could when the work was absent. The 2.87 s was therefore not simply the audits arithmetic time, and a cheaper check cannot claim it back.
noise_check: the baseline band across R147 to R156 is 17.902 to 18.092 s, so 18.650 s sits outside it and the regression is unlikely to be run-to-run noise, though each figure is a single run
consequence_for_the_status_document: the 0.65 s saving that R167 estimated for adopting the cheap check must be withdrawn. The status document has to stop offering the cheap audit as a way to buy step time.
decision_for_the_user: none needed; this candidate is rejected on measurement, so it no longer requires a decision
salvageable: the equivalence proof stands, and a cheaper check would only pay off if it also removes the per-layer serialisation, for example by batching the whole steps checks after the forward rather than per layer
